prompt: Match each place in a page to the encoding it needs.

pairs.right: HTML escaping, with the quotes kept

prompt: What is wrong with the idea of one `escape()` function for every place in a page?

choices.text: It is too slow to call everywhere on a busy page
choices.why: Speed is not the problem.

choices.text: Contexts need different encodings
choices.why: Right. Each context has its own reader and its own special characters; the encodings are not interchangeable.

choices.text: Python has no escape function
choices.why: markupsafe.escape exists; it is just not the only encoding.

choices.text: Escaping should happen at the input, once, before anything is stored
choices.why: At the input the destination is unknown; lesson 2 says why.

prompt: `json.dumps` writes a correct JavaScript string. Why is it not enough inside `<script>`?

choices.text: It does not escape double quotes
choices.why: It does: contexts.py printed \".

choices.text: Browsers cannot read JSON
choices.why: JSON is valid JavaScript.

choices.text: It leaves <, so </script> still ends the script
choices.why: Right. The HTML parser runs first, and it does not care about JavaScript strings.

choices.text: It escapes too much, and the note shows backslashes on the page
choices.why: It escapes too little for this place.

prompt: Why are the quotes around an HTML attribute part of the defence?

choices.text: Browsers refuse unquoted attributes
choices.why: Browsers accept them, which is the trouble.

choices.text: Without them, a space ends the value
choices.why: Right. An unquoted attribute ends at a space, which escaping leaves alone.

choices.text: Quotes make the attribute load faster
choices.why: No such effect.

choices.text: Quotes turn on escaping in Jinja, which is off for unquoted attributes
choices.why: Escaping is on either way; the quotes decide whether it is enough.

prompt: A patient's name goes into a search link inside href="…". Put the steps in the order the server applies them.
items: HTML-escape the whole URL for the attribute
write the attribute into the page

prompt: In a URL query, the character & is encoded as %___.
Why does an f-string encode nothing when it builds the page?

choices.text: It pastes text into text, without knowing it is HTML
choices.why: Right. Encoding needs to know the context, and an f-string knows none.

choices.text: f-strings were removed in Python 3.13
choices.why: They are alive and well.

choices.text: Flask turns escaping off for f-strings only
choices.why: Flask never sees the f-string; it receives the finished text.

choices.text: The values were already escaped in profiles.py
choices.why: They are stored raw, as they should be.

prompt: In the f-string page, `value="Lu "the fast""`. Where does the browser think the attribute ends?

choices.text: At the last quotation mark
choices.why: The parser stops at the first closing quote.

choices.text: After `Lu `, at the second quotation mark
choices.why: Right. The rest is read as something that is not an attribute.

choices.text: It never ends, and the page goes blank
choices.why: It ends early, which is worse than never.

choices.text: At the end of the line
choices.why: Line ends mean nothing inside a tag.

prompt: The note `back pain </script> again`, pasted into a script by the f-string, prints ` again";` on the page. Why?

choices.text: JavaScript does not allow the word again
choices.why: Words are not the issue.

choices.text: The note is longer than a script may be
choices.why: Length has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: Python printed it by mistake
choices.why: Python produced exactly the text it was given.

choices.text: The HTML parser ended the script at </script>
choices.why: Right. What follows is page text, whatever the JavaScript string intended.

prompt: How many of the six tests failed against the f-string page?
A website address `https://lucia.example/blog?a=1&b=2` sits correctly in an href. Why does a test still demand `&` there?

choices.text: Because the address is invalid without it, and browsers refuse to follow it
choices.why: The address is fine; the attribute is the context.

choices.text: In an attribute, & starts an entity
choices.why: Right. The browser turns & back into & before following the link.

choices.text: To stop the link from being clicked twice
choices.why: The link works the same.

choices.text: Because URL encoding requires it
choices.why: URL encoding would write %26; & is HTML's.

prompt: Why does `{{ p.note|tojson }}` have no quotes around it in the template?

choices.text: Jinja adds them later
choices.why: tojson adds them, as part of the literal.

choices.text: The filter writes them itself
choices.why: Right. Extra quotes would produce ""…"", a different bug.

choices.text: Notes cannot contain quotes
choices.why: They can; tojson escapes them.

choices.text: Scripts do not use strings
choices.why: This one assigns a string to const note.

prompt: Which function builds the search link's query in the fixed page?

choices.text: escape()
choices.why: escape is HTML's encoding; the query needs URL encoding first.

choices.text: tojson
choices.why: tojson writes JavaScript literals.

choices.text: url_for()
choices.why: Right. It URL-encodes the value, and autoescaping then escapes the URL for the attribute.

choices.text: an f-string
choices.why: That was the flaw.

prompt: What does `web_link()` add that escaping does not?

choices.text: It makes the link text bold so people notice it
choices.why: It changes nothing about the text.

choices.text: It encodes the address twice
choices.why: It encodes nothing.

choices.text: It checks that the website is online before drawing the link
choices.why: It makes no request.

choices.text: Only http and https become links
choices.why: Right. An allowlist of schemes: escaping makes the text harmless and says nothing about where the link goes.

prompt: A colleague writes `value={{ p.nickname }}`, without quotes, in the fixed template. What happens with the nickname `Lu "the fast"`?

choices.text: The attribute ends at the first space, escaped or not
choices.why: Right. The quotes are escaped and the space is not, so the value is cut at `Lu`.

choices.text: Nothing: autoescaping covers unquoted attributes as well as quoted ones
choices.why: It escapes quotes and angle brackets, not spaces.

choices.text: Jinja refuses to render the template
choices.why: Jinja renders it happily.

choices.text: The browser adds the missing quotes
choices.why: The browser reads what is there.

prompt: In a browser, what does the fixed page show in its heading?

choices.text: Lucia & Bia <3
choices.why: That is the source; the browser decodes the entities.

choices.text: Lucia & Bia <3
choices.why: Right. Correct escaping is invisible to the reader.

choices.text: Lucia
choices.why: Nothing is cut off anymore.

choices.text: An empty heading
choices.why: The heading is there, complete.

prompt: Which of these switch Jinja's escaping off for a value? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: the safe filter
choices.why: It marks the value as HTML.

choices.text: Markup(value) in Python
choices.why: The same, in code, and easier to miss in review.

choices.text: {% autoescape false %}
choices.why: It switches escaping off for a whole block.

choices.text: the tojson filter
choices.why: tojson encodes for JavaScript; it does not switch escaping off.

prompt: Where should data that a script needs go, instead of an onclick attribute?

choices.text: Into the onclick, HTML-escaped
choices.why: The JavaScript engine reads it after the entities are undone.

choices.text: A data- attribute, read from JavaScript
choices.why: Right. Data stays data, and the script reads it as a string.

choices.text: A style attribute
choices.why: CSS is another context with its own rules; keep user data out of it.

choices.text: A cookie
choices.why: Cookies are sent on every request; this data is for the page.

prompt: A template `email.txt` builds an HTML e-mail with the patient's name in it. What does Flask do with the name?

choices.text: Escapes it, as in every template
choices.why: Only some file names get autoescaping.

choices.text: Refuses to render HTML from a .txt file
choices.why: It renders whatever the template says.

choices.text: Nothing: .txt is not in the autoescaped list
choices.why: Right. .html, .htm, .xml, .xhtml, .svg and render_template_string are; .txt is not.

choices.text: Converts it to URL encoding
choices.why: No context is guessed from the content.

prompt: HTML is assembled in Python with an f-string and passed to the template with `|safe`. What went wrong?

choices.text: Nothing, if the template itself escapes
choices.why: |safe tells it not to.

choices.text: The page is rendered twice
choices.why: It is rendered once, without escaping.

choices.text: Every value inside skipped the escaping
choices.why: Right. Pass the values to the template and let it build the HTML.

choices.text: f-strings cannot hold HTML
choices.why: They hold any text, which is the problem.

prompt: Flask autoescapes templates whose names end in .html, .htm, .xml, .xhtml or .___.
A page writes `<a href="/exams?clinic={{ clinic }}">`, with autoescaping on. A clinic name `Moema & Sul` arrives. What is still wrong?

choices.text: Nothing: autoescaping covers it
choices.why: It covers the HTML layer, not the query.

choices.text: The value is not URL-encoded, so the query breaks at &
choices.why: Right. The inner layer is missing; url_for, or urlencode, adds it.

choices.text: The attribute needs single quotes
choices.why: Double quotes are fine.

choices.text: The value should be passed through tojson, which encodes it for any context
choices.why: That would put JavaScript quotes into a URL.

prompt: A message from the clinic must keep bold and italics, so the developer renders it with `|safe`. What does the course suggest instead?

choices.text: Escape it twice
choices.why: Then the formatting shows as tags.

choices.text: Use tojson instead
choices.why: That is for scripts.

choices.text: Trust it, since only staff accounts can write clinic messages
choices.why: Messages also come from patients, and staff accounts can be misused.

choices.text: Clean it to an allowed set of tags, as lesson 7 shows
choices.why: Right. Cleaning to an allowlist keeps the formatting without trusting the rest.

prompt: Match each output line from contexts.py to the call that printed it.
Why do escaping flaws survive for years in pages that seem to work?

choices.text: Browsers fix them automatically when they render
choices.why: Browsers read what they are given.

choices.text: Ordinary names lack those characters
choices.why: Right. Only a test with those characters shows the defect.

choices.text: Nobody uses quotation marks online
choices.why: People do, just not in most names.

choices.text: Escaping is checked by the database when the value is stored
choices.why: The database stores raw values, as it should.
